audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer read Skill for levels 1 through 6 while the content win[] rows and the packet levelChart both read Neeko for those five stages — five of seven rows rendering two different answers.
audit.why: Grounded in range and cooldowns rather than the chart: Blooming Burst reaches 800, Tangle-Barbs roots at 1000 on 12s, and Azir must stand at 525 to place a Sand Soldier with a 22s Shifting Sands as his only exit. Neeko owns the pre-item lane; Azir takes over at Nashor's, which is where both layers already agree.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side moved to Neeko with all five whys rewritten in the same proposal.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes and the level-6 prose described Azir's R as 'dive insurance' without naming what it insures against, and no Neeko spike was ever stated.
audit.why: Neeko's level 6 is Pop Blossom: 600 range, 120/105/90s, knock-up then a landing stun, and Riot's text says the preparation is hidden while she is disguised. Azir's are Nashor's Tooth and Emperor's Divide.
audit.corrected: spikes[0..3].text, breakdown.spikes, whys[4] and the content mid text now name Pop Blossom, its 600 range and the hidden wind-up.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page told you to 'sidestep it behind minions' — that is backwards. Riot's Tangle-Barbs text: 'If the tangle kills an enemy or passes through a champion, it becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer.' Standing behind a wave feeds it. The page also never mentioned Inherent Glamour's break conditions or Pop Blossom's hidden wind-up.
audit.why: Enemy E: 1000 range, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, roots everything it passes through and grows off any unit it kills. Enemy P: the disguise breaks on immobilizing CC, on Neeko casting a damaging spell, or once the disguise takes damage equal to its health bar — Azir's Q applies a slow, which is not immobilizing, so damage is the lever. Enemy R: preparation hidden while disguised. Owner E: 22/20.5/19/17.5/16s dash, and a root denies a dash outright, so her 12s root returns roughly twice per Shifting Sands.
audit.corrected: The minion advice is reversed and now says sidestep rather than hide; the disguise-break-by-damage mechanic and the hidden Pop Blossom wind-up are stated; the root-beats-dash cooldown ratio carries the trading and cooldown fields.

audit.why: 54.55% over 297 games. The packet flags this as contradicting a Neeko-heavy chart, but a scaling champion losing the first five stages and winning the game is consistent — the two are not in conflict.
Tangle-Barbs 12s at rank 1 / 1000 range; Shifting Sands 22s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with both numbers plus the growth-on-minion-kill clause.

edits.before: Neeko's burst poke and disguise trickery let her set up trades you won't see coming, punishing your immobile, cooldown-limited kit hard in this window. Be wary of jungle camps and minions that could be her in disguise, and avoid overextending since her burst combo can chunk you fast. Farm safely with W and don't contest her poke directly.
edits.after: Blooming Burst reaches 800 and blooms again when it kills units, so standing in the wave earns you the extra hit. Tangle-Barbs is worse than it looks: it grows larger and roots longer for every minion it kills, so hiding behind the wave is no plan — sidestep it. Check every ally and monster; a disguise breaks only once it takes its health bar in damage.

edits.before: Her ultimate is a powerful area-lock tool that can decide skirmishes and teamfights outright, so respect her all-in potential even after you hit 6, when your own R starts giving you a way to wall off her engage or peel. Focus on safe farming and side-wave pressure rather than direct duels in this stretch — her burst-heavy kit still edges you out in isolated fights. Look for opportunities to punish her when her key combo pieces are down.
edits.after: Pop Blossom knocks up and stuns everything within 600, and while she is disguised its wind-up is hidden, so at 6 the tell you normally rely on is gone — check every ally that walks at you. Your own R is the counter-engage: hold it for her landing rather than spending it on a wave. Farm side waves and punish the 12 seconds after Tangle-Barbs, the only window where she cannot start anything.

edits.before: Once you have your first item your poke and clear finally start to match her burst-poke hybrid profile, and by two items your zone control with R and soldiers clearly outclasses her more burst-reliant kit in extended fights. Build MR (Abyssal Mask) if she's snowballed kills, since her burst combo remains a threat into squishies. In teamfights, spread soldiers to deny her ultimate's full value and hold R to block her engage.
edits.after: Nashor's Tooth turns soldier autos into sustained damage her 12-second root cannot keep you away from, and by two items your soldiers out-range her whole kit. Build MR (Abyssal Mask) if she has snowballed, since the burst still kills squishies. In teamfights do not clump: Pop Blossom hits everything within 600 of her landing, and the wind-up is hidden if she is wearing an ally's face. Hold R for that landing.

edits.before: Play around her disguise to avoid ambush trades
edits.after: Damage suspicious allies to break her disguise

notes: Neeko is female; the shipped page used he/his/him in twelve fields. The single most valuable correction here is that the old advice to 'sidestep Tangle-Barbs behind minions' inverted the mechanic — Riot's text says the tangle becomes larger, faster and roots for longer if it kills a unit, so a wave makes it worse, not safer. That line appeared in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t and is fixed in all three. Also newly stated: Inherent Glamour breaks once the disguise takes damage equal to its health bar (Azir's Q slow is not immobilizing CC, so damage is the lever available to you), and Pop Blossom's preparation is hidden while she is disguised. Level chart disagreed across layers on rows 0-4 (full said Skill five times, content and packet said Neeko); full moved to match with all five whys rewritten in the same proposal. The packet suspectName on wants.foe[0] is a FALSE POSITIVE — Blooming Burst is the correct Q name — so that field is deliberately untouched. Ratings left alone: their semantics are inconsistent across this champion's matchups (see azir_mid__naafiri notes).
